title: Door lock control experiment (15 subjects, 4 classes, 31 EEG ch)
description: EEG dataset from 15 healthy participants performing an ERP-based (P300) brain-computer interface task for controlling a door lock, one of several home appliances in the original study. Thirty-one EEG channels were recorded at 500 Hz with an actiCHamp system while visual flash stimuli were presented in a 4-class oddball paradigm. Each subject completed 50 training and 30 testing blocks, with online visual feedback. The dataset supports research on P300 BCIs and inter-subject transfer learning.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a Brain Products actiCHamp active-electrode system (31 channels, 10-20 montage, linked-mastoid reference, 500 Hz). Participants viewed an LCD display with flashing visual stimuli (stimulus onset asynchrony of 750 ms) in a 4-class oddball paradigm. Target and non-target events were epoched over a 0-1 s interval. Each subject completed 50 training and 30 online testing blocks with visual feedback.
